findings.title: New rules validator is missing from the refusal registry
findings.description: `review_rules()` is a new validator in `tools/factory/agent.py` that refuses malformed rules files by raising `ValueError`. Its refusals are covered by `ReviewRulesPromptTest`, but the function is not listed in `GATES` in `test_gates_refuse.py`, and this PR does not modify that file. The name scan in `gate_functions()` matches only names containing entries from `NAME_PARTS`, such as `validate` and `parse`, and `review_rules` contains none of them, so the omission passes CI silently. A later change that weakens this validator would not be caught by the gate-refusal registry.

citations.citation: Keynes: gates are tested with inputs they must refuse

def review_rules(path: Path = REVIEW_RULES) -> str:
    """The rules only Qodo review enforces, as a Markdown list for the implement prompt.

    Raises ValueError when the file has no rules or a rule lacks a name or content, so the agent never
    runs with a silently empty rule list.
    """
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rules = data.get("rules") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(rules, list) or not rules:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no rules")
    lines = []
    for i, rule in enumerate(rules):
        name = rule.get("name") if isinstance(rule, dict) else None
        content = rule.get("content") if isinstance(rule, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip() or not isinstance(content, str) or not content.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: rule {i} has no name or content")
        lines.append(f"- **{name.strip()}** {' '.join(content.split())}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

evidence.explanation: The rule requires any new validator in tools/factory/ to be listed in GATES with refused inputs. `review_rules` raises on malformed input, so it acts as a validator. `test_gates_refuse.py` registers GATES entries by name, and `gate_functions()` only matches names containing the NAME_PARTS strings, which do not include `review_rules`. The PR does not modify `test_gates_refuse.py`.

findings.title: Code-fixing agents still never see the review rules
findings.description: The rules are injected only into the `implement` prompt in `run.py`, while the other prompts that make Codex write code after review (`fix-review`, `fix-checks` in `run.py`, and `fix-pr`, `fix-update`, `fix-checks` in `watch_prs.py`) receive no rules. The fix runs are where Qodo's review-only findings are typically addressed, so the agent that writes the fix can still violate "errors fail loudly" or the other 13 rules.

findings.title: Prompt test checks only rule names, not their text
findings.description: `test_implement_prompt_names_every_rule_in_the_rules_file` asserts only that each rule's name appears in the rendered prompt, so a regression that drops or truncates `content` would still pass. The test cannot tell whether the rule body Codex needs actually reached it.

citations.citation:
def test_implement_prompt_names_every_rule_in_the_rules_file(self):
        import json
        rules = json.loads(agent.REVIEW_RULES.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["rules"]
        prompt = self.render_implement()
        self.assertNotIn("{review_rules}", prompt)
        for rule in rules:
            with self.subTest(rule=rule["name"]):
                self.assertIn(rule["name"], prompt)

evidence.explanation: The loop asserts only `rule["name"]` in the prompt. The renderer produces `- **name** content` for each rule, so a loss of the content field would not fail any assertion.

findings.title: Rules reach Codex without their good and bad examples
findings.description: `review_rules()` emits only each rule's `name` and `content`, dropping `good_examples` and `bad_examples`, which hold the concrete silent-fallback and fail-loud patterns. Codex therefore receives an abstract rule text without the concrete shapes Qodo flags, which weakens the stated purpose of getting the rule into the agent before review.
